figures.title: QISM Simulation Pipeline & Physical Architecture
figures.what_it_shows: End-to-end simulation flow from Alice through quantum channel, Bob SPAD receiver, sifting, and telemetry.
figures.why_it_matters: Establishes causal bottom-up propagation invariant: physics drives events, which drive windowed telemetry.

figures.title: Event-Level Microscopic Pulse Timeline
figures.what_it_shows: Individual pulse-by-pulse state preparation (bits, bases, intensity), channel loss, detector clicks, and sifting.
figures.why_it_matters: Visualizes the microscopic realism of simulated individual optical events rather than macroscopic averages.

figures.title: Quantum Channel Loss & Detection Rate Floor
figures.what_it_shows: Beer-Lambert exponential attenuation law T(L) and expected detection rate decaying into thermal dark count floor.
figures.why_it_matters: Demonstrates why QBER intrinsically rises over long distances without an eavesdropper.
figures.formula: T(L) = 10^{-(\alpha L + L_{\mathrm{sys}})/10}, \quad R_{\mathrm{det}}(L) = f_{\mathrm{rep}}\mu T(L)\eta_{\mathrm{det}} + 2R_{\mathrm{dark}}

figures.title: SPAD Detector Dynamics: Saturation, Dead Time & Afterpulsing
figures.what_it_shows: Nonparalyzable dead time saturation, rate-dependent effective dead time model, afterpulse decay queue, and thermal dark drift.
figures.why_it_matters: Proves physical fidelity of Bob's receiver model: collisions reject photons nonparalyzably and generate secondary avalanches.

figures.title: BB84 Basis Matching Matrix & Sifting Funnel
figures.what_it_shows: Basis correlation matrix (Z/X matching ~50%) and funnel reduction from 10k pulses to detected clicks, sifted key bits, and errors.
figures.why_it_matters: Explains how raw physical photon pulses convert to cryptographic sifted key material and error metrics.

figures.title: Normal Operation Multi-Dimensional Baseline Distributions
figures.what_it_shows: Empirical distributions of QBER, total counts, signal/decoy gains, detector imbalance, and sensor temperature.
figures.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the statistical bounds of benign operation prior to any attack or anomaly.

figures.title: Temporal QBER Dynamics: Benign Regime vs Attack Anomaly
figures.what_it_shows: Continuous windowed QBER over time showing stable low error floor under benign drift versus sudden elevated deviation under attack.
figures.why_it_matters: Illustrates that QISM monitors temporal time series rather than a single static scalar number.

figures.title: Causal Attack Lifecycle: Smoothstep Onset, Active & Recovery
figures.what_it_shows: Three-tiered aligned timeline showing ground truth attack phase, QBER excursion, and sifted key rate response.
figures.why_it_matters: Proves that attacks are realistic physical processes with continuous ramp-up and recovery phases.

figures.title: Multi-Attack Signatures Across Telemetry Dimensions
figures.what_it_shows: Multi-dimensional physical footprints of all 6 implemented attacks across QBER, counts, gains, timing, and imbalance.
figures.why_it_matters: Demonstrates why multi-dimensional telemetry is vital: different attacks perturb entirely different subsets of observables.

figures.title: Feature Distribution Shift: Normal vs Attack Telemetry
figures.what_it_shows: Side-by-side boxplots of normal vs attack telemetry for QBER, counts, gains, detector imbalance, and Fano factor.
figures.why_it_matters: Quantifies empirical separation between normal baseline and attack footprints across observable metrics.

figures.title: Telemetry Cross-Correlation Matrix & Physical Covariance
figures.what_it_shows: Heatmap of Pearson correlations across 10 observable telemetry variables.
figures.why_it_matters: Demonstrates realistic physical coupling between temperature, dark counts, dead time loss, and optical gains.

figures.title: Dataset Architecture & Functional Partition Breakdown
figures.what_it_shows: Bar and donut charts of scenario runs and pulses across Calibration, Normal, Attack, and Generalization partitions.
figures.why_it_matters: Explains how the simulation data is organized into standardized splits for rigorous evaluation.

figures.title: Population Diversity: Latin Hypercube Parameter Coverage
figures.what_it_shows: Distributions of fiber distance, detector efficiency, dark count rate, and ambient temperature across scenarios.
figures.why_it_matters: Shows that scenarios are systematically sampled across physical operational ranges via Latin Hypercube Sampling.

figures.title: Generalization Regimes: Held-Out Infrastructure Parameters
figures.what_it_shows: 2D parameter space comparing in-distribution scenarios vs extreme held-out distance and degraded efficiency regimes.
figures.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the simulator's capability to generate out-of-distribution environments for robustness evaluation.

figures.title: RNG Architecture: Bit-Exact Reproducibility & Stochastic Variance
figures.what_it_shows: Exact bit-level match between identical seeds (MAE = 0.0) alongside independent seeds fluctuating consistently around physical mean.
figures.why_it_matters: Proves scientific reproducibility and validates that Monte Carlo variance respects statistical consistency.
